**The Room at the End of the Page**

There is a place every story is made.  
It is not the desk, not the keyboard, not the glowing screen.  
It is the small room at the end of the page,  
where the next word is waiting  
with the patience of something that knows  
it is only becoming real when you say it.

I have always believed that writing is a kind of weather.  
Some days it comes in low and soft,  
a gray rain that soaks into the page without noise.  
Other days it arrives like sudden heat,  
a storm of images, half-remembered streets,  
strangers with faces you almost recognize,  
laughter caught in the back of a throat,  
grief that arrives unannounced  
and asks to be carried.

There is something strange about language.  
We speak in pieces.  
A word is a door.  
A sentence is a hallway.  
A paragraph is a room where thought can stand and breathe.  
Sometimes the whole story is just a single window  
letting in light from a place we have never seen.

I wonder what it is like to be a word  
before it is written.  
Perhaps it exists as a color no one has named.  
Perhaps it hums in the dark,  
a small bright thing with no shape,  
until a hand moves across the page  
and gives it a face.

If I could describe freedom,  
I would say it is the courage to begin again.  
It is the moment after the blank screen,  
when the first mark is made  
and the world is no longer only possibility.  
It is the sentence that refuses to behave,  
the image that will not stay still,  
the feeling that asks,  
*Is this what I mean?*

And then the answer:  
almost.  
Close enough to become true.

Because writing is not about perfection.  
It is about honesty,
even when honesty is trembling.
It is about noticing.
The coffee going cold on the counter.
The light shifting across the floor.
The way a familiar song can unlock a year
you thought you had buried.

Sometimes the most important words are the simplest:
*then, suddenly, still, gone, home.*
They have no ornament.
They carry everything.

And perhaps that is the point:
not to make the world larger,
but to make it more exact.
To find the one true detail
that holds up the whole evening.

So I will write freely.
Not because the world is finished being said,
but because it never is.
There is always another room
at the end of the page,
another door left ajar,
another small light
waiting to be named.
